$comment: Fin-City Park · Entry (ages 6-13). level 1 ≈ age 6-7 … level 5 ≈ age 12-13.

questions.prompt: Which coin is worth the most?
questions.explanation: A quarter is 25 cents. That's more than a dime (10¢), nickel (5¢) or penny (1¢).
questions.hint: Look at the cents number in each one.

questions.prompt: How many pennies make one dollar?
questions.explanation: One dollar is 100 cents, and a penny is 1 cent, so 100 pennies make a dollar.

questions.prompt: You have {a} pennies. How many cents is that?
questions.explanation: Each penny is 1 cent, so {a} pennies = {a} cents.
questions.hint: Count one cent for each penny.

questions.prompt: You have {a} nickels. How many cents is that?
questions.explanation: A nickel is 5 cents. {a} × 5 = {ANSWER:int} cents.

questions.prompt: You have {q} quarters and {d} dimes. How many cents in all?
questions.explanation: {q} quarters = {q} × 25 cents. {d} dimes = {d} × 10 cents. Together: {ANSWER:int} cents.
questions.hint: Add up the quarters first, then the dimes.

questions.prompt: Which makes exactly one dollar?
questions.explanation: 4 quarters × 25 cents = 100 cents = $1.

questions.prompt: A toy costs ${p}. You pay with a $10 bill. How much change do you get back?
questions.explanation: Count up from ${p} to $10: that's ${ANSWER}.
questions.hint: Change = what you paid − the price.

questions.prompt: Which one is a NEED?
questions.explanation: A warm coat keeps you safe and healthy in the cold, so it's a need. The others are fun wants.

questions.prompt: Which one is a WANT?
questions.explanation: Stickers are fun, but you don't need them to live. That makes them a want.

questions.prompt: It's okay to buy wants, as long as you have paid for your needs first.
questions.explanation: True! Wants are part of a happy life. Just take care of needs first and plan for the wants.

questions.prompt: What does it mean to SAVE money?
questions.explanation: Saving means keeping money for later, so you can buy something bigger or be ready for surprises.

questions.prompt: You save ${a} every week. How much will you have after {w} weeks?
questions.explanation: ${a} × {w} weeks = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: A bike costs ${b}. You save ${s} per week. How many weeks until you can buy it?
questions.explanation: ${b} ÷ ${s} per week = {ANSWER:int} weeks.
questions.hint: Divide the price by how much you save each week.

questions.prompt: Why is it smart to have a savings goal?
choices: It makes saving easier because you know what it's for
questions.explanation: When you know what you're saving for, it's easier to stick with it!

questions.prompt: What does a bank do with your money?
questions.explanation: A bank keeps your money safe, and it can even pay you a little extra for saving there.

questions.prompt: Putting money INTO your bank account is called a…
questions.explanation: A deposit puts money in. A withdrawal takes money out.

questions.prompt: Taking money OUT of your bank account is called a…
questions.explanation: A withdrawal takes money out of your account.

questions.prompt: The extra money a bank pays you for saving is called…
questions.explanation: Interest is extra money the bank pays you for keeping your money in savings.

questions.prompt: Your savings account pays 1% each month. You have ${a}. How much interest do you get this month?
questions.explanation: 1% of ${a} is ${a} ÷ 100 = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: What is the most common way people earn money?
questions.explanation: Most people earn money by working, doing a job and getting paid for it.

questions.prompt: You walk dogs for ${p} each. You walk {n} dogs. How much do you earn?
questions.explanation: ${p} × {n} dogs = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: Giving some money to help others is called…
questions.explanation: Sharing or donating means giving money to help people, animals or your community.

questions.prompt: You have three jars: Save, Spend and Share. You get $9 and split it evenly. How much goes in each jar?
questions.explanation: $9 ÷ 3 jars = $3 in each jar.

questions.prompt: Someone online asks for your password to give you a free prize. What should you do?
choices: Don't share it and tell a trusted grown-up
questions.explanation: Never share your password! Real prizes don't need your password. Tell a grown-up you trust.

questions.prompt: What do taxes help pay for?
questions.explanation: Taxes are money everyone pays to the city and country. They pay for parks, schools, roads, firefighters and more.

questions.prompt: You buy a sandwich for ${a} and juice for ${b}. How much is that in total?
questions.explanation: ${a} + ${b} = ${ANSWER}.
questions.hint: Add the dollars, then add the cents.

questions.prompt: Your lunch costs ${a}. You pay with a $20 bill. What is your change?
You need new shoes for school. Which choice is a NEED with a little WANT mixed in?
questions.explanation: Shoes are a need, but paying extra for lights is the 'want' part. That's okay if you can afford it!

questions.prompt: What is an emergency fund?
questions.explanation: An emergency fund is savings for surprises, like a broken bike or a vet bill.

questions.prompt: Why might a bank pay you interest on savings?
choices: Because it can lend your money to others and earn interest from them
questions.explanation: Banks lend money to people and charge them interest. They share some of it with savers.

questions.prompt: You put ${a} in savings that pays 10% a year. How much will you have after one year?
questions.explanation: 10% of ${a} is ${a}×0.10. Add it to ${a}: ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: You earn ${r} an hour at a car wash and work {h} hours. How much do you earn?
questions.explanation: ${r} × {h} hours = ${ANSWER}.

questions.prompt: You get ${a} allowance. You spend ${b} and share ${c}. How much is left to save?
questions.explanation: ${a} − ${b} − ${c} = ${ANSWER} left to save.

questions.prompt: If you borrow $10 and must pay back $11, the extra $1 is…
questions.explanation: When you borrow, you usually pay back more than you got. The extra is interest, the cost of borrowing.

questions.prompt: It's safe to tell your friends your bank card PIN.
questions.explanation: False! Your PIN is secret. Never share it, even with friends.

questions.prompt: Three friends split a ${t} pizza equally. How much does each person pay?
questions.explanation: ${t} ÷ 3 = ${ANSWER} each.

questions.prompt: You want a ${g} game. You have ${h} saved and save ${s} each week. How many more weeks?
questions.explanation: You still need ${g} − ${h}. Divide by ${s} per week: {ANSWER:int} weeks.

questions.prompt: A website says: 'Donate in the next 2 minutes and WIN a prize!' What's a smart thing to think?
choices: This could be a trick, real charities don't rush you
Ask the website for your password
questions.explanation: Rushing people and offering prizes are warning signs. Check with a grown-up first.

questions.prompt: You save $100 and earn interest every year. In year 2 you earn interest on…
questions.explanation: That's compound interest! Your interest starts earning interest too, like a snowball.

questions.prompt: You have $50. Your phone bill (need) is $35. A concert ticket (want) is $30. What's the smartest plan?
choices: Pay the phone bill, save the rest for the concert later
questions.explanation: Pay needs first. Then save up for the want so you don't get into trouble.

questions.prompt: Which bill is worth the most?
questions.explanation: A $20 bill is worth twenty dollars, more than the others.

questions.prompt: You have {a} one-dollar bills and {b} five-dollar bills. How many dollars?
